title: Reflection Loops
summary: Use explicit critique and revision cycles to improve a draft against measurable criteria, while avoiding unsupported confidence from repeated self-assessment.
overview: Reflection loops evaluate an agent's draft or execution result and feed actionable feedback into a revision step. The evaluator may be a separate model, deterministic checks, a human rubric, or a combination. The key distinction is that a critique identifies a concrete defect and an acceptance criterion; asking the same model to think harder is not a reliable architecture.

Repeated model agreement does not establish truth because correlated errors can survive every pass. Anchor reflection in external evidence, schema checks, or executable tests. Preserve the original artifact and each revision so operators can detect when a superficially polished version introduces factual regression.

production.poc: A prototype can compare first drafts with one revised draft on a labeled evaluation set. Keep the loop only if improvement exceeds the added latency and cost.
production.production: Production separates factual checks from style preferences, caps revision attempts, and prevents a critic from broadening the task. Revisions must revalidate evidence references and mandatory content.
production.scale: At scale, route only likely-defective artifacts through expensive critique. Track defect classes, critic precision, revision acceptance, and cases where the original draft was better than the revised result.

components.name: Draft producer
components.role: Creates an initial artifact with explicit evidence and output requirements.

components.name: Rubric evaluator
components.role: Identifies localized defects against versioned criteria and records supporting observations.

components.name: Revision worker
components.role: Applies bounded corrections without changing accepted facts or expanding authorized actions.

components.name: Comparison gate
components.role: Checks regressions and selects the best validated version rather than always choosing the latest.

components.name: Revision ledger
components.role: Stores artifact versions, critique reasons, outcomes, and consumed budget.

flow.title: Establish rubric
flow.description: Define what correctness, completeness, and presentation mean for this particular artifact.

flow.title: Create baseline
flow.description: Generate and retain the first draft with its source evidence and configuration versions.

flow.title: Evaluate defects
flow.description: Apply deterministic checks first, then use a critic where semantic judgment is necessary.

flow.title: Request targeted revision
flow.description: Send specific defects and protected facts, with a maximum change scope and budget.

flow.title: Check regressions
flow.description: Re-run factual and structural validation and compare the revised artifact against the baseline.

flow.title: Accept or escalate
flow.description: Publish a validated version or expose unresolved defects when the revision ceiling is reached.

diagrams.caption: The original remains available, and a later draft is accepted only after passing the same evidence checks.

useCase.title: Reviewing a patient-facing appointment letter
useCase.situation: A hospital scheduling service produces letters that combine appointment instructions, location details, and accessibility information.
useCase.problem: Initial drafts can omit preparation instructions or introduce confusing phrasing even when the source schedule is correct.
useCase.requirement: The assistant must improve clarity and completeness while preserving verified times, locations, and clinician-approved instructions.
useCase.architecture: A draft generator uses approved records; deterministic checks protect critical fields, and a semantic critic evaluates readability and missing requirements.
runtime: The first draft is checked against a letter rubric, and a missing transport-access note becomes a targeted revision request.
The revised letter is compared with the original, with appointment facts checked again before staff release.
useCase.failure: If the critic recommends an unsupported preparation instruction, the evidence gate rejects that change and retains the verified draft.
useCase.impact: Measure omission rate, introduced factual errors, revision acceptance, and staff editing effort. The loop supports communication quality, not clinical decision authority.

tradeoffs.benefit: A focused rubric can uncover defects missed during drafting.
tradeoffs.cost: A second model can share the same misconceptions.
Cost and latency grow, while later changes can regress accuracy.

tradeoffs.benefit: Protected fields remain stable through stylistic changes.
tradeoffs.cost: Semantic errors outside the checks still require evaluation.

failures.detection: Feedback lacks a rubric item or supporting source.
failures.recovery: Reject the critique and retain the prior validated artifact.

failures.detection: Ledger records repeated reversals without defect reduction.
failures.recovery: Select the best validated version and stop the loop.

mistakes.fix: Ground checks in evidence or independent test criteria.
Compare validated versions and preserve the best result.
Specify defects, protected facts, and stopping conditions.

whenToUse: Artifacts have clear rubrics and measurable defect classes.
One revision produces demonstrable quality improvement.
The workflow can afford additional evaluation latency.
whenNotToUse: No external criterion distinguishes improvement from preference.
The task requires immediate response with no revision budget.
The same ungrounded model is the only source of truth.
checklist: Measure critic precision and introduced errors.
